V

The story

18 min · reading

Read one part at a time, aloud. Words with a dotted line have a translation — put your mouse on them. After each part, answer: What is different now?

❖

Part one · The merchant’s daughters

Once upon a time, there was a rich merchant. He lived in a big house with his three daughters. The youngest daughter was called Beauty, because she was kind, gentle, and very beautiful. But people loved her not only for her face. They loved her because she listened, helped others, and never thought she was better than anyone else.

Her two older sisters were different. They liked beautiful dresses, expensive things, and rich men. They often laughed at Beauty because she enjoyed simple things: reading books, walking in the garden, and spending time with her father.

One day, the merchant lost all his money. His ships disappeared at sea, and he had to sell the big house. The family moved to a small house in the country. The two older sisters were angry and unhappy. They complained every day.

“This life is terrible,” they said. “We were born for better things.”

But Beauty did not complain. She helped in the house, cooked food, cleaned the rooms, and worked in the garden. At first, this life was hard for her too, but she tried to stay calm and useful.

Part two · One rose

After some time, the merchant heard good news. One of his ships came back to the city. He hoped he could get his money again. Before he left, he asked his daughters what presents they wanted. The older sisters asked for dresses, jewels, and expensive shoes.

Beauty smiled and said, “Father, I don’t need anything. But if you see a rose, please bring me one.” Her sisters laughed. “A rose? How simple.”

The merchant went to the city, but his hope did not last long. The ship was not his anymore, and he did not get his money back. He was sad and tired. On his way home, he got lost in a dark forest. Snow began to fall. The wind was strong, and he could not see the road.

Then he saw a light far away. He followed it and found a large castle. The doors were open, but no one was there. Inside, it was warm and beautiful. There was a fire in the fireplace and a table with hot food.

The merchant was afraid, but he was very hungry. He ate the food and slept in a comfortable room. In the morning, he found clean clothes and breakfast waiting for him. “This castle is strange,” he thought, “but someone here is very kind.”

Before he left, he walked through the garden. Even though it was winter, he saw a beautiful rose bush. He remembered Beauty’s wish and picked one rose.

Part three · The Beast’s price

Suddenly, he heard a terrible voice. “Who told you that you could take my rose?”

The merchant turned around and saw a Beast. He was huge and frightening. His face was not human, and his eyes were dark and sad. The merchant fell to his knees. “Please forgive me. I only wanted to bring this rose to my youngest daughter.”

The Beast looked at him for a long moment. “You took my rose after I gave you food, warmth, and a bed. You must pay for this.”

The merchant was shaking. “Please, sir. I have daughters. Let me say goodbye to them.”

The Beast answered, “You may go home. But you must return in one month. Or one of your daughters must come here instead of you.”

The merchant was horrified, but he promised. The Beast gave him a horse and a bag of gold, and the merchant went home.

When he arrived, Beauty was happy to see him, but she quickly understood that something was wrong. Her father told the family everything. The older sisters cried loudly, but Beauty saw that they were not really worried about their father. They were worried about losing their comfortable life again.

“This is my fault,” Beauty said. “You picked the rose for me. I will go to the castle.”

Her father refused, but Beauty was calm. “You are old and tired. I cannot let you die because of a flower.”

Part four · Dinner every evening

One month later, Beauty went to the castle. When they arrived, the doors opened by themselves. Then the Beast appeared. “Did you come by your own choice?” he asked. “Yes,” she said. Her voice was quiet, but she did not look away.

The next morning, Beauty said goodbye to her father. She watched him ride away, and for the first time, she felt truly alone.

But the castle was not cruel to her. Every day, she had beautiful rooms, warm food, books, music, and dresses. Invisible servants took care of everything. In the evenings, the Beast came to dinner. At first, Beauty was afraid of him. He was large, strange, and his voice was deep. But he was never rude to her.

“Do you think I am very ugly?”

Beauty did not want to lie. “Yes,” she said slowly. “But I think you are kind.” The Beast was silent. Then he said, “That is more important.”

At the end of every dinner, he asked the same question: “Beauty, will you marry me?” And every evening she answered gently, “No, Beast. I am sorry.” He always looked sad, but he never became angry.

Months passed. Beauty was still a prisoner, but she did not feel hated or unsafe. She began to wait for their evening talks. She liked his honesty.

Part five · Seven days

One night, Beauty had a dream about her father. He was ill and alone. In the morning, she begged the Beast to let her visit him. “My father may be dying. Please let me go.”

The Beast looked hurt, but he gave her a ring. “You may go for one week. Put this ring on the table before you sleep, and you will wake up in your father’s house. But you must come back after seven days. If you do not return, I will die of sadness.”

Beauty promised. The next morning, she woke up at home. Her father was ill, but when he saw her, he became stronger.

Her sisters came to visit too. They were shocked when they saw Beauty’s fine dress and calm face. They thought she had a wonderful life in the castle. They were jealous.

“Stay longer,” they said sweetly. “Father needs you.”

Beauty wanted to return to the Beast, but her sisters cried and begged. She stayed one more day. Then another.

Part six · In the garden

On the tenth night, Beauty had a terrible dream. She saw the Beast lying in the garden near the rose bush. He was not moving. Beauty woke up in fear.

“What have I done? He trusted me.”

She put the ring on the table and wished to return to the castle. In the morning, she was there. She ran through the rooms, calling for the Beast. He did not answer. At last, she found him in the garden, just like in her dream.

Beauty fell beside him. “Beast, please wake up. I came back. I am sorry.”

The Beast opened his eyes. “You forgot me,” he whispered.

“No. I was foolish and afraid. I thought I only cared for you as a friend. But when I thought you were dead, I understood the truth. I love you.”

The Beast looked at her with surprise. “Then will you marry me?” — “Yes. With all my heart.”

Part seven · The spell breaks

At that moment, the castle filled with light. The Beast disappeared, and in his place stood a prince. He was young, handsome, and human again. Beauty stepped back in shock. “Where is the Beast?”

The prince smiled sadly. “I am the Beast. A fairy put a spell on me because I was proud and selfish. I had to learn kindness and find someone who could love me for my heart, not my face.”

Beauty looked at him for a long moment. “I loved the Beast,” she said softly. “So I hope the prince is as kind as he was.”

The prince took her hand. “I will try to be worthy of you.”

Soon after that, Beauty and the prince were married. Her father came to live near the castle, and he was happy again. Beauty did not forget her old life, and she did not forget the lonely Beast in the garden.

She understood something important: a beautiful face can hide a cold heart, and a frightening face can hide a gentle one. And love, when it is real, sees more than the eyes can see.

Eight key sentences

4 min · key sentences

Turn the cards and read them aloud. Then close them and tell the story again with only these eight sentences.

❖
VIII

Let’s talk

10 min · speaking

Answer like this: your opinion → the reason → an example. Try to use the new words.

❖
Faces

The story says a beautiful face can hide a cold heart. Do you agree? Why?

I agree / I don’t agree, because…

Choice

Beauty goes to the castle for her father. Was this a good choice, or was it too dangerous?

In my opinion, it was… because…

The Beast

The Beast keeps Beauty in his castle. Can we call him kind? What is good and what is bad about him?

He is kind when… But he is not kind when…

Sisters

Why are the sisters jealous? Is jealousy always a bad thing?

They are jealous because… Sometimes jealousy…

Promise

Beauty promises to return in seven days, but she stays longer. Is it always necessary to keep a promise?

I think we must… but sometimes…

You

Think of a person you did not like at first, but later you changed your opinion. Tell the story.

At first I thought… but then…

Homework

2 min
❖
  • Write 80–100 words. Beauty writes a letter to her father from the castle, after her first dinner with the Beast. What does she see? How does she feel? Use six new words.
  • Speak (send me a voice message, 1–2 minutes). Tell the story again. Use the eight key sentences as your plan.
  • Find and write. Find five irregular past simple verbs in the story (for example: saw). Write the infinitive too: see → saw.
